comment: The cross-language conformance suite -- TEST-010, anchored at Proposal 2.4 (NN-4, 'Multi-Language by Design').
Proposal 2.4 makes three commitments this file exists to make checkable:
1. 'WIT is the source of truth' -- every language binds from wit/, so the WIT surface is a
conformance obligation for every language, and each obligation names the checker that
enforces it. A case whose checker is not registered in BOTH gates is a case nothing enforces.
2. 'No privileged language' -- the reference application is implemented five times and all five
3. 'Parity is measured' -- 'Any gap requires a written exception with an owner and a date'.
The third commitment is the one that decays. A gap with no owner is a gap nobody owns, and a
matrix that lists them without an owner is a document that reports a problem and assigns it to
no one. tools/check_conformance.py fails on exactly that, and on a status that disagrees with the
STATUS IS DERIVED, NOT DECLARED-AND-TRUSTED. 'supported' must agree with build::toolchain_for
returning Some; 'gap' must agree with it returning None. When LANG-009..040 land and a language
starts building, CI fails here until this file is updated -- which is the point of LANG-040.

cases.summary: every wit/ interface parses, so every language can bind to it
every wit/ file is embedded in qqq-abi, so the runtime can serve what a language binds to
every interface carries @since, so a binding cannot silently track a moving contract
every fallible call returns a typed error, so a binding does not decode a status code
no hidden global state, so a binding cannot read configuration the manifest never granted
the six WIT style rules of Proposal 6.3, so five hand-written bindings stay comparable
the artifact is a component rather than a core module, so the runtime can instantiate what the toolchain produced
every qqq: interface the guest imports maps to a capability, so no import reaches past the capability model
